A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TRACE research work. Their complete main text, tables, figures, equations, and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval, forecasting, classification, ablation, and runtime experiments in the main text and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including cross-modal and time-series retrieval, downstream prediction, ablations, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The encoder, channel identity tokens, channel-biased attention, alignment losses, and RAG procedure are unchanged. The expanded Section 3.4 restates RAG construction and training details already present in v1 Appendix D.5.

E1.justification: Both use the curated weather dataset and TimeMMD Health, Energy, and Environment subsets for the same tasks. v2 Section 4.3 relocates the time-series retrieval evaluation already reported in v1 Appendix D.8.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across the corresponding experiments. In particular, ED, DTW, SAX-VSM, and CTSR all appear in both v1 Table 11 and v2 Table 2.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, training settings, model configurations, and evaluation metrics are retained. The cross-modal comparison still uses 2,000 query pairs, and the relocated time-series retrieval comparison still uses 1,000 randomly sampled queries.

E4.justification: The architectural and hyperparameter ablations, hard-negative analyses, embedding visualizations, retrieval case studies, and efficiency analysis are retained. Moving the quantitative retrieval comparison into the main text adds no new analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five runs with different random seeds in Section 4.1 and retain the same uncertainty displays, including the ± entries in the attention-ablation table. No statistical reporting procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: Matched tables and figures retain their numerical results and qualitative findings. For example, TRACE retains time-series retrieval P@1 of 0.900, MRR of 0.938, and query time of 0.045 seconds in v1 Table 11 and v2 Table 2.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and alignment equations in Section 3 and Appendix C, and the complexity reasoning in Appendix D.9, are unchanged. The added notation in Section 3.4 restates the existing Appendix D.5 formulation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about multimodal alignment, benchmark contributions, dual encoder/retriever utility, and downstream performance. Greater prominence for time-series retrieval does not broaden the existing contribution claims.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and limitations concerning aligned textual supervision and computational overhead remain unchanged. The more detailed future-work passage in v2's conclusion already appeared in v1 Appendix E, which is retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds a first-page footnote identifying the TRACE code repository. Hyperparameters, hardware, data processing, and detailed RAG settings remain unchanged; the expanded main-text RAG explanation was already documented in v1 Appendix D.5.

R1.justification: The same 59 cited works and substantive research positioning are retained. SAX-VSM changes from reference 59 to reference 57 as its discussion moves into the main text; it is not a newly cited work.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites Section 3.4, promotes the quantitative retrieval discussion from Appendix D.8 to Section 4.3, and repeats existing appendix future-work material in the conclusion. It also adds acknowledgments and updates venue information; most prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v1 Table 11 is relocated and resized as v2 Table 2. The attention-ablation table and Figure 5 are enlarged, with associated text reflow and table renumbering. All ten figures retain their underlying content.

improvement.justification: v2 makes existing RAG details and time-series retrieval evidence easier to find, enlarges the hard-negative ablation display, and supplies a TRACE code location. These modestly improve clarity and reproducibility guidance while the methods, empirical evidence, and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
